title: Student identity linked to submission data
description: The student's identity (via login credentials and student ID) can be linked to their assignment submission data (work file, course, timestamp), creating a persistent association between the student and their academic work.
assumptions: The system stores and processes both identity and submission data in a way that allows correlation.

title: Assignment submission data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The Grades Portal Web App may expose student submission data (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) to unauthorized users or systems, violating confidentiality requirements.
assumptions: The system has inadequate access controls or data protection measures for submission data.

title: Unauthorized submission usurpation
description: An attacker could potentially submit assignments on behalf of a student by exploiting authentication weaknesses, leading to false attribution of academic work.
assumptions: The authentication mechanism has vulnerabilities or the system lacks proper verification of student identity during submission.

title: Transmission of Student Identifiers to Grading Service
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits student id, course, and file reference to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2), creating a flow of identifying information between processes.
assumptions: Student identifiers are transmitted in clear or insufficiently protected form during the P1→P2 flow.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.2.1.1 from context applies to identifier threats; confidence in this specific application is moderate.

title: Processing of Identified Student Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) processes identified data including student id, course, and file reference received from the portal, enabling identification of students within the grading system.
assumptions: P2 processes the received identifying data for grading purposes without additional anonymization.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.1.1 from context applies to processing of identified data; confidence moderate.

title: Non-repudiation of Submission and Grading Requests
description: The flow transmits requesting role and submission data, creating evidence that could prevent students or instructors from denying their involvement in specific grading or submission actions.
assumptions: The system logs and retains evidence of who submitted what and when, creating non-repudiable records.
uncertainty_note: Context [4] describes non-repudiation as a threat type; specific tree node Nr.1.1 inferred based on standard LINDDUN Pro structure.

title: Excessive Personal Data Collection in Assignment Storage
description: The Assignment & Grading Service stores student ID, course, and submission time with each assignment file. This represents explicit data disclosure by design. The threat is whether this data collection is minimal and necessary, or if it exceeds what's required for the grading function.
assumptions: Student ID is personally identifiable information; course information may be linked to other student records
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is inferred from context about data disclosure; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary

title: Student Identifiability Through Stored Assignment Data
description: Storing student ID with assignment files creates identifiability risk. The combination of student ID, course, and submission time could allow identification of the student, especially if assignment content is also stored or if this data is accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Student ID is a direct identifier; course information may be used to narrow identification
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is inferred; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary

title: Data Integrity Risk for Stored Assignment Records
description: Assignment files containing student ID, course, and submission time could be tampered with or altered after storage. This threatens the integrity of academic records and could lead to false attribution of work.
assumptions: Stored data could be modified by unauthorized actors or system errors
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is inferred; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary

title: Linkability of Assignment Data with Other Student Records
description: The stored assignment data (student ID, course, submission time) could be linked with other student records or systems, potentially creating a comprehensive profile of the student's academic activity beyond the intended scope.
assumptions: Student ID serves as a linking key across multiple data stores or systems
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is inferred; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary

title: Processing of identifiable student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes student submission data that contains personally identifiable information. When teachers request the queue of submissions, they access data that could identify individual students, including names, course associations, and potentially other identifying details.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: Student submission data accessed by teachers could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if access controls are not properly implemented, potentially violating student privacy and exposing sensitive academic information.

title: Teacher account impersonation during login
description: The teacher's login process could be vulnerable to credential theft, phishing, or session hijacking, allowing unauthorized actors to impersonate teachers and access the submission queue.

title: Linkability of submissions to students and courses
description: The system may reveal patterns that allow linking submissions to specific students, courses, or teachers, potentially enabling inference attacks that could expose additional privacy-sensitive information.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: Student personal information (names, work content, submission times) displayed to teacher could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties if teacher account is compromised or if teacher shares data inappropriately with colleagues or students.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a reasonable tree node for disclosure threats in Process→ExternalEntity flows based on context [3][4].

title: Unauthorized access to student submission data
description: Student submission data could be accessed by unauthorized individuals if the teacher's credentials are compromised, if there are insufficient access controls on the portal, or if the teacher's device is insecure.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as a reasonable tree node for usurpation threats in Process→ExternalEntity flows based on context [3][4].

title: Non-compliance with student data privacy regulations
description: Sharing student personal information with teachers must comply with FERPA/GDPR regulations. Inappropriate sharing, lack of proper consent, or failure to implement required safeguards could result in regulatory violations.
uncertainty_note: Using Nc.1.1 as a reasonable tree node for non-compliance threats in Process→ExternalEntity flows based on context [3][4].

title: Teacher Identity Usurpation
description: An attacker could impersonate a teacher to record grades or feedback for students, potentially submitting malicious or incorrect grades.
assumptions: Teacher credentials are not adequately protected; authentication system has vulnerabilities.

title: Grade and Feedback Disclosure
description: Grades and written feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties, potentially revealing student performance or teacher evaluation patterns.
assumptions: Data transmission or storage lacks proper access controls; data is accessible to unauthorized users.

title: Grade or Feedback Tampering
description: An attacker could alter recorded grades or feedback text, potentially affecting student records or teacher accountability.
assumptions: Data integrity controls are insufficient; no proper audit trail or validation mechanisms.

title: Student and Teacher Identification
description: Student IDs and grader IDs in the flow could be used to identify specific students and teachers, potentially leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: IDs are not properly anonymized or masked; data is accessible to unauthorized parties.

title: Grade Recording Non-Repudiation
description: A teacher could deny having recorded a specific grade or feedback, potentially leading to disputes or lack of accountability.
assumptions: No proper audit logging or digital signatures are in place to establish non-repudiation.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: The grading service writing to the Grade Records Database could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties, exposing sensitive student grades and personal information.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls on the database or network transmission
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a representative disclosure threat node for Process→DataStore flows

title: Student and Grader Identification
description: Grade records contain student id and grader id, which could be used to identify specific individuals and their academic performance.
assumptions: Student and grader IDs are not properly anonymized or protected
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a representative identification threat node

title: Linkability of Student Data
description: Grade records could be linked with other student data (e.g., enrollment records, personal information) to create comprehensive profiles of students.
assumptions: Student IDs are used consistently across multiple systems without proper isolation
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a representative linkability threat node

title: Grade Record Tampering
description: Grade records could be altered or corrupted during the write operation, potentially changing grades or feedback without proper audit trails.
assumptions: Insufficient integrity controls or audit logging on the database
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a representative data degradation threat node

title: Database-Level Unauthorized Disclosure
description: The Grade Records Database itself could be accessed by unauthorized entities, exposing all stored grade records.
assumptions: Database lacks proper access controls, encryption, or audit mechanisms
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a representative disclosure threat node for DataStore

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation
description: Storage of student grades and personal information may violate data protection regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if proper safeguards are not implemented.
assumptions: Data handling practices do not meet applicable privacy regulations
uncertainty_note: Using Nc.1.1 as a representative non-compliance threat node

title: Linkability of student identity to grades
description: The system can link the student's identity to their grades and feedback through the request-response interaction, potentially enabling correlation of this data with other datasets.
assumptions: The system maintains records that associate student identity with grade data.

title: Identifiability through grades data
description: Grades and feedback are personally identifiable information that can reveal the student's identity, especially when combined with other contextual data.
assumptions: Grades are unique to each student and can be used to identify them.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades
description: Grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage, violating student privacy expectations.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or encryption could expose grades to unauthorized access.

title: Usurpation of student's grade access
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the student to access their grades and feedback, or the system could be tricked into granting access to unauthorized users.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be bypassed or compromised.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades during transmission
description: Grades and teacher feedback transmitted from the portal to the student could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly secured.
assumptions: Network traffic is not encrypted or authentication mechanisms are weak
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a reasonable node for disclosure threats at flow level

title: Linkability of grades to student identity
description: The displayed grades could be linked to the student's identity, potentially enabling correlation with other data sources to build a comprehensive profile of the student.
assumptions: Student identity is associated with the displayed grades
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 is a standard node for linkability threats at destination

title: Usurpation of student account access
description: If a student's credentials are compromised, an attacker could impersonate the student to access their grades and feedback, potentially for academic fraud or identity theft.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are not sufficiently robust
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a standard node for usurpation threats at source

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's grades to third parties
description: Parent's request for child's grades could result in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive educational data to third parties if authentication or access controls are insufficient.
assumptions: Parent account has proper authorization to access child's grades

title: Parent account impersonation during login
description: Parent could be impersonated during login process, allowing unauthorized access to child's grades and other sensitive information.
assumptions: Authentication mechanism may be vulnerable to credential theft or phishing

title: Grades data manipulation by unauthorized actor
description: Grades data could be altered or tampered with by unauthorized actors if the system lacks proper integrity controls.
assumptions: System has insufficient data integrity mechanisms

title: Linkability of parent identity to child's grades
description: Parent's identity could be linked to child's grades data, potentially revealing sensitive family relationships or educational patterns.
assumptions: System logs or metadata could enable identity linking

title: Linkability of child's academic data to other profiles
description: The parent receiving grades, feedback, and submission history could potentially link this data to other information about the child (e.g., medical records, behavioral data, or other school records), creating a comprehensive profile that exceeds the intended scope of the grades portal.
assumptions: Parent has access to other data sources about the child; data is not sufficiently anonymized or compartmentalized.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a reasonable choice for linkability threats in Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's academic information
description: The grades, feedback, and submission history displayed to the parent could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through account compromise, data logging, or improper access controls on the portal.
assumptions: Parent account credentials could be compromised; system may log sensitive data; access controls may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a standard disclosure threat node for Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Usurpation of parent identity to access child's grades
description: An unauthorized actor could usurp the parent's identity (e.g., through credential theft, social engineering, or account takeover) to gain access to the child's grades, feedback, and submission history.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be weak; parent identity verification may be insufficient; session management may have vulnerabilities.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is appropriate for identity usurpation threats in Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Non-compliance with FERPA and privacy regulations
description: The disclosure of child's grades, feedback, and submission history to the parent may not fully comply with FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act) or other applicable privacy regulations regarding student data protection and parental access rights.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements may be complex; data handling may not meet all compliance standards; audit trails may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Nc.1.1 is a reasonable choice for non-compliance threats in educational data contexts.

title: Administrator Account Usurpation
description: School Administrator (EE4) has privileged access to create, modify, and disable accounts. An attacker could impersonate the administrator to gain unauthorized access to the Grades Portal Web App (P1), potentially compromising all student and parent data.
assumptions: Administrator credentials are not adequately protected; no multi-factor authentication or session management controls.

title: Sensitive PII Disclosure via Administrator Actions
description: Administrator creates/modifies accounts containing names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships. Unauthorized disclosure of this sensitive PII could occur through improper access controls, logging, or data transmission.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without adequate encryption; access logs may expose sensitive information.

title: Account and Relationship Data Tampering
description: Administrator can modify account data and parent-child relationships. Malicious or compromised administrator could alter student records, parent relationships, or role assignments, leading to data integrity violations.
assumptions: No adequate audit trails or integrity checks on modifications; administrator actions are not logged or monitored.

title: Non-repudiation of Administrator Actions
description: Administrator actions (creating/modifying accounts) may lack proper audit trails, allowing the administrator to deny performing specific actions. This could lead to accountability issues and inability to trace data modifications.
assumptions: System lacks comprehensive logging; actions are not cryptographically signed or timestamped.

title: Administrator Identity Linkability
description: Administrator's actions and identity could be linked across multiple data flows or sessions, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of administrator behavior patterns.
assumptions: System logs and metadata may contain identifiable information linking administrator to specific actions.

title: Unauthorized Access to Account Records
description: Account records and parent-child relationship links written to the Account Directory could be accessed by unauthorized users or systems, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: The Account Directory lacks proper access controls or authentication mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard security practices may not be fully implemented

title: Identification of Students and Family Members
description: Account records containing parent-child relationship links could be used to identify students and their family members, potentially revealing sensitive family structure information.
assumptions: The data contains personally identifiable information that can be linked to real individuals.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the granularity of the account records stored

title: Data Manipulation of Account Records
description: Account records written by the grading service could be altered, deleted, or corrupted by unauthorized actors, compromising data integrity and potentially affecting student records.
assumptions: The Account Directory is accessible to systems or users without proper authorization.
uncertainty_note: Assumes insufficient access controls on the data store

title: Disclosure During Data Write Operation
description: The grading service writing account records to the directory could expose sensitive data during the write process, potentially through logging, monitoring, or interception.
assumptions: The write operation is not properly encrypted or secured during transmission.
uncertainty_note: Assumes the write channel may lack proper security measures

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external Cloud Hosting Provider (EE5) as part of nightly backup and replication. This represents explicit disclosure of personal data across organizational boundary to a known third party.
assumptions: The cloud hosting provider has access to all student personal data including grades, assignments, and account information.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 selected based on context [5] describing data disclosure as transfer to third party; this is the most applicable node for explicit disclosure scenario.

title: Linkability of Student Records Across Systems
description: Grade records and account directory data transferred to EE5 could be linked with other data sources to create comprehensive profiles of students, potentially enabling cross-system tracking of individuals.
assumptions: The cloud provider may have access to additional data sources or the data could be correlated with other datasets.
uncertainty_note: Linkability threat is inherent in any PII transfer but severity depends on what other data the provider has access to.

title: Identification of Students via Account Directory
description: Account directory data transferred to EE5 contains personally identifiable information that could be used to directly identify students/users without additional context.
assumptions: Account directory includes names, IDs, or other identifiers that can be used to identify individuals.
uncertainty_note: Assuming account directory contains identifiable information; severity depends on specific data elements included.

title: Grade Records Enable Student Identification
description: Grade records contain personally identifiable information that can directly identify students, parents, and teachers when accessed by the grading service.
assumptions: Grade records include student IDs, names, and contact information

title: Grade Records Enable Linkability Across Views
description: Grade records can be linked across student, parent, and teacher views, potentially revealing relationships and patterns that could be exploited for profiling.
assumptions: Views share common identifiers that can be correlated

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records may be accessed by unauthorized parties if the grading service lacks proper access controls or if data is transmitted insecurely.
assumptions: Access controls may be insufficient or misconfigured

title: Excessive Data Collection for Views
description: Building student, parent, and teacher views may require collecting more grade record data than necessary for the intended purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Views may include historical grades or additional metadata beyond what's needed

title: Usurpation of Student/Parent Identity
description: Unauthorized individuals may impersonate students, parents, or teachers to access grade records if authentication mechanisms are weak.
assumptions: Authentication may not properly verify user identities

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Educational Data
description: Handling of grade records may violate FERPA, GDPR, or other educational privacy regulations if data is not properly protected or consent is not obtained.
assumptions: Data handling may not comply with applicable privacy laws
